title: Bromoviridae Coverage Audit
eyebrow: LowVan · Bromoviridae module · 29 September 2026 · rescue backfilled 1 October 2026 · ORF1a, RdRp and accessories 2 October 2026
h1: Does the cucumber mosaic virus module actually work?
standfirst: Bromoviridae is a tripartite plant-virus family built at family level because all five genera share the layout: RNA1 carries 1a, RNA2 the RdRp and in the cucumoviruses 2b, RNA3 the movement protein and the coat protein. Cucumber mosaic virus, brome mosaic virus, alfalfa mosaic virus, tobacco streak virus. It routes 74.2% of complete genomes, and the remaining 25.8% receive no annotation at all — that is an accepted limit, closed on 30 September 2026, not outstanding work.

sections.title: What the module covers
sections.lede: Tripartite, so one genome arrives as three records and must be merged.

blocks.html: Every BV-BRC record carries contigs=1, so a genome is deposited as three separate records sharing a name and merge_segments.py is mandatory at annotation time.

sections.title: How it was built
sections.lede: The naming trap: the source calls two different proteins “replicase”.

blocks.html: 1a and 2a are different proteins on different segments, and the source calls both replicase. That string is therefore not binned on the word at all — it is routed to REP1 or REP2 by length against the two measured medians, and anything far below either is left unbinned rather than assigned to whichever is nearer.
§08 is about what happened when that routing was given no margin.

sections.title: Where the cutoffs sit
sections.lede: 400 for 1a, 300 for the RdRp, 80 for the structural proteins.

blocks.html: REP2's max_len was 993 aa and is now 900. The old value was exactly REP1's median length, which is the whole of §08 in one number.

sections.title: Does it route?
sections.lede: 74.2% of complete genomes. One genome in four gets nothing.

blocks.html: This figure was re-measured from scratch on 30 September 2026 because neither number previously reported could be substantiated. 94.8% came from --merge-by-name, which collapses records sharing a genome name; that is right for the three segments of one multipartite genome but it also merges independent isolates deposited under one name, and 55 of 1,264 Bromoviridae names carry more than three records. 69.5% appeared in the prose of this page and in the build notes with no recorded computation behind it at all.

The measurement that stands: 2,964 segment records of at least 2 kb assemble into 600 complete three-segment genomes (merge_segments.py refusing the 63 name collisions and 144 incomplete sets), which fall into 130 clusters at 70% nucleotide identity. 25 references reach 445 of them.

A three-way split would reach about 90%. Given each genus its own 25-reference budget: Cucumovirus 335 genomes over 40 clusters → 95.5%; Ilarvirus 162 over 67 clusters → 74.1%; Alfamovirus, Bromovirus and Anulavirus together 98 genomes over 20 clusters → 100%. Weighted, 90.4% against 74.2% lumped.

Cucumovirus is the natural boundary because it is the one real organisational difference in the family: it carries the 2b silencing suppressor on RNA2 and the other four genera do not, which is why P2B is called on 50.0% of routed genomes and correctly carries no copy_num.

Closed, 30 September 2026. Shipped at 74.2% by the curator's decision, not split. 155 of 600 complete genomes — 25.8% of the family — match no reference and so receive no LowVan annotation whatsoever: not a wrong call, no call. A three-way split would reach about 90% and remains available if that becomes worth doing; it is recorded here as a known and accepted cost rather than a pending task.

P2B is the cucumovirus 2b silencing suppressor and is genuinely absent from the other genera, so its 50% is biology and it correctly carries no copy_num. Every assignment in the shipped module was already right.

sections.title: Are the calls right?
sections.lede: 89.2% genuinely clean — after the fix in §08. Before it, 43.9%.

blocks.html: The duplicate-call audit is now completely empty: no exact duplicates, no nested calls.

One genome in four of this family is not annotated by this module. 155 of 600 complete genomes match none of the 25 references, so the annotator never reaches them and they carry no features at all. Everything in §05 and §06 — the call rates, the 89.2% clean — describes only the 445 that did route. Read the two together: a high quality score on a partial denominator is not a high quality score on the family.
No mature peptides. Neither 1a nor 2a has cleavage sites documented for this family in a form that can be located from the sequence.
The evaluation is a sample — 148 genomes at ≥6 kb, seed 29. Routing in §04 is a census.

The homology rescue has now run on this module. Completed 1 October 2026, closing the item deferred on 30 September. rescue_unassigned.py takes every protein no annotation-string rule matched, blastp’s it against this module’s own collections and adopts each into the feature it matches at ≥80% identity over ≥60% of the query, refusing everything below that rather than sweeping it into a grab-bag. It had never run on this module because it crashed on the trailing tab BV-BRC writes into uniq.seq. 816 of 1253 unassigned sequences were adopted; the training set went 2904 → 3568 sequences (+23%) and the profile set 124 → 135. Exactly neutral, and only after a correction. Four 993-aa sequences annotated RNA-dependent RNA polymerase entered REP2; blastp puts them at 97–99.6% identity to REP1 across all 993 residues, so they are 1a proteins mislabelled at source. They raised REP2’s max_len from 886 to 993 and produced a profile that called the 1a ORF a second time, flagging Too many contigs for RNA2 on 8 genomes. Removed to REP2.rejected_1a.fasta. The check that catches this: REP2 held no sequence above 900 aa before the rescue and four after — a collection whose maximum length jumps is a binning change, not a coverage gain. Measured against a control — the shipped module scored on the same 139 genomes with the current JSON — the rescue moved genuinely-clean from 84.9% to 84.9% (0 genome(s) improved, 0 regressed). The earlier comparison against measurements/quality.tsv was discarded: that table predates the 30 September copy_num and vocabulary edits, which on some modules dominate the rescue entirely. And it re-opened the defect §08 describes. The rescue adopted one more 993-aa 1a into REP2, and three others were put back by hand because REP2.fasta held 587 sequences against a build log saying 590 — the three §08 had deliberately removed. All four raised max_len to 993 again and cost 8 genomes to Too many contigs for RNA2 before they were caught. Removed to REP2.rejected_1a.fasta; max_len restored to the 900 this section records. The one-line check that catches it: REP2 held no sequence above 900 aa before the rescue and four after. A collection whose length extremes move has had its membership changed, not merely extended — count, min and max, never count alone.

1 accessory features were added, 2 October 2026. The unassigned pool had never been clustered for this module — UNASSIGNED_TRACKING.tsv recorded it and nothing downstream read the file. Running the kit's own accessory_clusters over it (mmseqs at 25% identity) produced homology groups that a string rule cannot reach: on Velarivirus, 21 sequences all exactly 157 aa with half of them labelled hypothetical protein. Groups that produced no profile are deliberately not declared, and groups measured to be homologous to each other were merged — a first pass ran at a member floor of 5 against the kit's default of 12 and over-split seven features across three modules.

Measured on the same 142 genomes scored after the homology rescue: genuinely clean 84.9% → 86.3%, features called 579 → 627 (2 genome(s) improved, 0 regressed). The new accessories carry no copy_num, so they name proteins without counting against the verdict — which is why the clean rate can hold while the feature count rises sharply. What this does not show is whether the new calls are right. It shows they fire, do not collide and trip no quality check; whether a group is one protein correctly identified is a curation question.

sections.title: What the run found
sections.lede: Two profiles calling one gene, on a third of all genomes.

blocks.html: REP1 and REP2 were called on identical coordinates in 32% of genomes. They are 1a and 2a — different proteins on different segments — so sharing coordinates is not merely suspicious, it is impossible.

blocks.text:
REP2 collection   n=590   median 840 aa   max 993 aa
REP1 collection   n=293   median 993 aa   min 908 aa

3 of REP2's 590 members hit REP1 at 97% identity / 100% coverage
REP2 max_len was 993 -- exactly REP1's median length

blocks.html: Three 1a sequences had been binned into the REP2 collection. They formed their own cluster, produced their own profile, and that profile fired on 1a — and REP2's length window, whose ceiling was exactly REP1's median, admitted the call. The module's own build notes warn that the source calls both proteins “replicase”; the length routing that was supposed to separate them had no margin at the top.

Removing the three sequences, rebuilding REP2 (587 sequences, 29 profiles) and tightening max_len to 900 took the module from 43.9% to 89.2% genuinely clean and eliminated the duplicate calls entirely.
Fixed. Three contaminating sequences and one length ceiling, worth 45 points of genome quality.

The routing gap was accepted rather than fixed. The three-way split that would take the family from 74.2% to roughly 90% is measured, documented and undone. That was a judgement about where effort goes, made with these numbers in hand, and it applies to this family only.

The module's vocabulary is complete after two genomes. The source reaches 49 distinct strings with its knee at 132 and is still climbing — and among those strings is the bare word replicase standing for two different proteins, which is what §08 is ultimately about.
